chunks: Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
The holder of a deposit and the holder of merchandise are both entrusted.

key_terms.الْبِضَاعَةِ: merchandise or goods given to someone for handling or trade
key_terms.الْوَدِيعَةِ: a deposited item entrusted to someone's care
key_terms.صَاحِبُ: the possessor or holder responsible for the entrusted item
key_terms.مُؤْتَمَنَانِ: two persons regarded as entrusted and trustworthy

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a person entrusted with a deposit or merchandise in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes that a person entrusted with a deposit or entrusted goods is regarded as a trustee. It indicates a legal and ethical principle in financial dealings: such a person is fundamentally treated as trustworthy in the absence of proof to the contrary.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4087 - Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:
"The trustee of a deposit (wadi'ah) and the trustee of merchandise (bida'ah) are both considered trustworthy."
